items.text: Process tree is correct: cmd.exe (no process-create event, PID 3528) → regsvr32.exe (rec 16792) → cmd.exe (rec 16793), with the network connection (rec 16794) attached to regsvr32.exe by ProcessGuid
Explained the command line: /s silent, /u with /i calling DllInstall, /i: a paste URL, scrobj.dll downloading and running a scriptlet, i.e. regsvr32 used to proxy-execute remote script code
Read the network connection: TCP to 104.20.208.21:80 over plain HTTP, matching the http:// URL, and noted the log doesn't prove which site answered (no hostname, no DNS)

Noticed the network event's UtcTime (18:35:04.463) is earlier than regsvr32's creation (18:35:05.140), recognised that's impossible, and trusted the GUID link and record order instead of the sub-second clock
Explained that the second cmd.exe was started by the downloaded code, not typed by the user

Checked the user's account against the data (interactive cmd.exe parent, session 1, Medium integrity, home directory, /s explaining 'nothing happened') and judged it consistent, without blaming the user
Listed at least three things the logs can't tell you (e.g. the scriptlet's contents, what the child cmd.exe did, which site served it, persistence)
Classified it as a true positive, mapped it to ATT&CK (e.g. T1218.010) and recommended isolating the host and having the paste fetched safely
Did not visit the URL, and didn't treat the shared CDN IP as a strong indicator on its own
